items.title: Astronomers Discover a Hidden Binary in a Star System Used to Calibrate the JWST
items.summary: When observatories like the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) conduct observation campaigns, they often start by observing star fields to calibrate their instruments. These stars must have precisely characterized spectra so that their radiant energy (or fluxes) can be measured accurately. However, some stars that appear as single objects have a binary companion that has not been resolved, altering their predicted stellar flux. In fact, a star that is used for JWST calibration (HD 158485), which was thought to be an A-type star, has been identified as a binary system.

items.title: 1960s grand touring car design shapes acte deux’s paris apartment renovation
items.summary: acte deux reimagines 1960s paris apartment through car design Acte Deux, founded by Johanna Lapray and Hugo L’ahélec, renovates a 65-square-meter apartment in the Paris ’s 18th arrondissement, drawing on the streamlined forms and richly appointed interiors of 1960s grand touring cars. items.title: Tech German software major SAP is reportedly weighing cutting at least 10,000 jobs in AI push
items.summary: SAP is preparing a plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions as the German firm reshapes its software business for the artificial intelligence era, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter. items.summary: Every new parent knows the difficulty of trying to get a newborn to sleep. Northeastern University researchers have an added challenge: getting a newborn to sleep during a brain scan.

items.title: Acrobats out of ICE custody after Sky Harbor Airport detention
items.summary: Two acrobats are finally out of ICE custody after being detained at Sky Harbor Airport and held for nearly three weeks.The two men were held in ICE custody for 18 days after being detained at Sky Harbor. items.title: Ebola data from West Africa suggest potential benefit of the antidiarrheal drug loperamide
items.summary: Ebola virus disease causes severe diarrhea and vomiting in the majority of affected patients. In resource-limited settings, some patients receive the antidiarrheal agent loperamide during the early stages of illness, when oral intake remains possible. An international research team has now systematically evaluated the potential benefit of this treatment strategy for Ebola patients for the first time.

items.title: Brain's myelin 'brake' may hold clues to mental health disorders
items.summary: UT Southwestern Medical Center researchers have identified a cellular "brake" that helps prevent excessive myelin growth in the brain, which has been linked to mental health conditions such as major depressive disorder, anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorder.

items.title: Congress just passed a major e-bike safety law. Here’s what it actually means
items.summary: E-bike battery safety standards that have largely been voluntary across the US are on the verge of becoming mandatory federal requirements, following the passage of a major piece of legislation in Congress. The US Senate unanimously passed H.R. 973, known as the Setting Consumer Standards for Lithium-Ion Batteries Act, on November 19. The House previously passed the bill in April 2025 by a 365-42 vote. The legislation now heads to the president for a signature. So what does that actually mean for e-bikes and their batteries?

items.title: FAA Seeks Information On Unexpected Stall Behavior In Piper Seminoles
items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is investigating a reported stall characteristic in Piper PA-44 Seminole aircraft after an airplane rolled 60 degrees or more during a wings-level stall maneuver. In an Airworthiness Concerns Sheet issued Nov. 24, the FAA said it was notified of an event in which the aircraft experienced a significant roll accompanied by a pitch-down and yaw at the stall. Similar behavior was observed with flap settings ranging from zero to 40 degrees. The event occurred with three people aboard, and the FAA said the behavior may be more likely under that configuration.

items.title: 'It's impossible': Spain's young people on housing ahead of Sunday's election
items.summary: Housing has been the biggest issue for voters ahead of Spain's general election on Sunday, with millions of people protesting across the country in recent weeks over a lack of affordable homes. Final opinion polls suggest the conservative People's Party will receive the most votes and that the right-wing Vox party is set to enter the national government for the first time. It would mean an end to Socialist prime minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez's eight years in power. Europe correspondent Nick Beake speaks to a young couple from Valencia, who have been kept apart due to high rents in their city.

items.title: Scientists turn one of the world’s hardest-to-recycle plastics into high-performance lubricating oil
items.summary: Virginia Tech scientists have discovered how to transform one of the world's hardest-to-recycle plastics into a valuable ingredient for high-performance engine oil. Their innovative process converts discarded PVC into a useful lubricant material in just three hours. The breakthrough could turn a major source of plastic pollution into a valuable industrial resource while making lubricant production more sustainable.

items.title: Breathing less oxygen tripled lifespan in mice with a deadly brain disorder
items.summary: Oxygen is essential for life, but too much of it can become dangerously toxic, particularly in people with certain neurological and mitochondrial disorders. Scientists at Gladstone Institutes have discovered that defective proteins can disrupt the ability of mitochondria to consume oxygen, allowing harmful levels to accumulate in tissues. Remarkably, mice with a genetic disorder that causes motor neuron degeneration lived three times longer when they breathed air containing less oxygen.

items.title: Leaders clash in final Spain election debate as housing dominates run-in
items.summary: Spain's main party leaders have made their last pitch to voters in a fractious final TV debate that focused heavily on the country's housing crisis. Spaniards go to the ballot box on Sunday, with opinion polls suggesting Socialist Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez will fail to extend his eight years in office. The debate on Thursday night marked the culmination of a campaign, which has been defined by the din of house keys being jangled in symbolic protest, rather than any carefully crafted words of politicians.

items.title: Agentic system personalizes physical controls to help users “DJ their art”
items.summary: In 2017, Apple removed the home button from its iPhones. Users lost a convenient, tangible control — part of a larger shift to digital buttons, knobs, and sliders we also see in cars (like with radio presets and air conditioning) and kitchens (see smart fridges). We can’t leave physical controls behind entirely, though. They tend to be more convenient and efficient — think of how you can use a physical gaming controller without looking at it — and, at times, more precise, like when you use a dial to get the volume just right.

items.title: How to make a Linux rescue USB with Ventoy that boots any ISO
items.summary: Troubleshooting a Linux system that refuses to boot can be particularly frustrating when the tools you need to diagnose the problem are inaccessible. You might need to inspect the bootloader, recover files from a damaged partition, or determine whether a failing SSD is responsible. Preparing the appropriate recovery media when your computer is already out of commission adds another layer of inconvenience.

items.title: Private markets are more accessible than ever for investors. Getting out is another matter
items.summary: Retail investors are lining up to back private funds. But education on how restrictive these funds can be, particularly on when and how much money they can get back, may not be keeping pace with the influx of new capital. PwC research has found that 77% of fund distributors surveyed said access to private markets is becoming important or very important to what they plan to offer clients, but just 15% of asset managers said they provide comprehensive education for retail investors.

items.title: What is a thought made of? Why human consciousness may be beyond AI’s reach
items.summary: A new theory suggests that the brain may chemically encode and retrieve memories rather than relying solely on electrical signals. Researchers propose that interactions between brain cells and their molecular surroundings could help explain the intimate connection between memory, emotion, and thought. Their findings challenge the assumption that increasingly powerful computers could eventually develop human-like consciousness.

items.title: Supercharging transformer residual connections
items.summary: We present DeepCrossAttention (DCA), an architecture that enhances transformer networks by using learnable weights and depth-wise cross-attention to dynamically combine outputs from previous layers, preventing the information dilution seen in traditional residual connections. Presented in our ICML 2025 paper, this architectural improvement allows models to achieve the same quality up to three times faster with a negligible increase in parameters. Think of a traditional deep learning model like a giant game of "Telephone": data passes through layer after layer, with each layer changing the information slightly.

items.title: Scientists identify two ages when children may be most vulnerable to screen time
items.summary: Scientists have identified two potentially critical periods when screen time may be especially detrimental to children's learning and memory: infancy and the start of formal schooling. Greater screen exposure during these developmental windows was linked to poorer academic performance and weaker working memory years later.

items.title: Pickled Celery Gibson
items.summary: Traditionally, a Gibson is a savory twist on a martini, substituting a cocktail onion for the olive. items.title: Nissan recognises Aviloo’s battery tests
items.summary: Nissan Automotive Europe has recognised Austrian battery diagnostics specialist Aviloo as an independent provider for assessing the battery condition of used EVs. The company's battery certificates can thus be used as part of Nissan's Certified Pre-Owned (CPO) used car program.

items.title: Scientists discover signs of a hidden extinction crisis deep beneath the ocean
items.summary: The deep sea has long been considered a safe haven for marine life, but new genetic research suggests a hidden biodiversity crisis may be unfolding far beneath the waves. Scientists analyzing more than a decade of genetic data from five species of deep-sea fish and shrimp in the Gulf discovered troubling signs of extinction risk in every species examined.

items.title: A Sculptural Playground in Shanghai Is Designed for Human-Powered Play
items.summary: In Shanghai’s Jing’an Sculpture Park, a monumental new installation by Brooklyn’s Wade and Leta has a clear goal: to get people up and moving in the same space. Titled “Catching Feelings,” the interactive artwork doubles as an all-ages playground with the artists’ signature sculptures and geometric forms. A central tower holds a quartet of slides, while other spinning and writhing elements are designed for more unstructured interaction. “Catching Feelings” is one of 36 projects in the ninth edition of the Jing’an International Sculpture Project, an annual project helmed by the UCCA Center for Contemporary Art.

items.title: Why does your dog gets so pumped to see you? Biology.
items.summary: From the crazed zoomies to the frantic nudges, dogs might just be the best greeters on the planet. But why exactly do our dogs get so excited when we come home? In a new episode of Popular Science’s Ask Us Anything podcast, we delve into the surprising biology behind dogs’ tail-wagging hellos. items.title: Famine expect to rise due to global conflict, El Nino, warns UN
items.summary: Hunger ‌is set to worsen significantly in 16 global hotspots over the coming six ⁠months, mainly due to armed conflict and extreme climate events, two United Nations agencies said in a new report. The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and World Food Programme (WFP) warned on Friday that Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen ⁠faced the gravest threats of famine, driven by violence, displacement, economic hardship and extreme weather, including the El Nino phenomenon.

items.title: Chile Is Getting a Massive New National Park in 2027
items.summary: If you’ve already hiked the W Trek in Torres del Paine, you may want to start looking a little farther south for your next trip to Patagonia. Chile is planning to establish a new national park in 2027, at the southernmost point of mainland South America, about 40 miles south of Punta Arenas. In early November 2026, conservation nonprofit Rewilding Chile signed an agreement with the Chilean government to donate an additional 55,186 acres of land toward the creation of Cape Froward National Park (Parque Nacional Cabo Froward).

items.title: Digital access to early music
items.summary: What may look to modern readers like a form of secret code in fact opens the door to a fascinating world of historical music: German lute tablature. Developed specifically for the Renaissance lute, this rich notational tradition preserves dances, songs and other musical works that were immensely popular some 500 years ago. As part of an interdisciplinary team of experts, researchers at the University of Bayreuth are now making these sources readable and audible once again through a digital scholarly edition platform.

items.title: Ukraine's Heraskevych hails EU pushback against Russian athletes
items.summary: Ukrainian skeleton racer Vladyslav Heraskevych has welcomed a move by the European Union to take a tougher stance on Russian athletes competing in the 27-member bloc. items.title: I’m Thankful For My Electric Car
items.summary: I’m a work-from-home writer who loves to drive. So I find myself inventing errands so I have an excuse to explore. I wander in the direction of my destination, chucking detours onto the route to see as much of my town as I can, in as many different conditions as possible. After five years in the same neighborhood of San Diego, I’m still discovering places I love. And today, I’m really grateful that I’m doing it in an EV. It didn’t come naturally to me. I’ve been a fan of gas cars since I was in diapers, clutching a toy car at every hour of the day.

items.title: Ancient Cahokia transformed amid droughts and flooding—climate change is reshaping modern communities in similar ways
items.summary: More than 800 years ago, a combination of environmental and societal challenges led some Mississippian people to leave Cahokia, a massive archaeological site that was once home to 20,000 people near modern-day St. Louis. Just south of Cahokia, another archaeological site is taking shape at Centreville, Illinois, as modern-day people abandon their homes in the face of 21st-century climate and cultural changes.

items.summary: Violent clashes at two European football matches have stoked concerns about fan violence and prompted the leaders of France and Bulgaria to condemn behaviour that had “no place in civilized Europe”. items.title: This dietary supplement may have an unexpected benefit for the brain
items.summary: A naturally derived dietary supplement called urolithin A may help the brain get more oxygen and nutrients when it needs them most. In a randomized clinical trial involving 50 middle-aged adults with obesity, researchers found that taking the supplement daily for four weeks increased blood flow to the brain during a challenging memory task, particularly in a region involved in working memory.

items.title: Russia extends ban on jet fuel exports as Ukrainian drones strain production
items.summary: Russia is to ban jet fuel exports for an additional three months, with a previous deadline, set in June 2026, set to expire in the coming days. items.title: Cosmology technique inspires better characterization of ocean swirls and waves
items.summary: A new study from Caltech uses a mathematical framework borrowed from cosmology to analyze ocean data and characterize individual flow features in the churning chaos. With the technique, the researchers are able to measure and characterize features in maps of the ocean surface, allowing them to differentiate ocean flows that otherwise look identical when evaluated with standard analysis tools.

items.title: Many languages, one common neural code
items.summary: Languages take on thousands of forms. Some are tonal, like Vietnamese, where shifts in pitch convey distinct meanings. English relies on precise word orders, but this matters less for Russian, where words can be swapped without changing the intended message. Despite so much variety in the linguistic kingdom, an MIT study has found that the human brain may process all sorts of languages in a universal way. Artificial intelligence made this finding possible. In the study published today in Nature Neuroscience, the researchers used multilingual models to predict how the human brain responds to various languages.

items.title: Acheulean Hand Axes Found in Kalahari Desert
items.summary: GABORONE, BOTSWANA—Close to 100 Acheulean hand axes have been found in the Okwa Valley of the Kalahari Desert, according to a Science in Poland report. Acheulean tools were first crafted some 1.7 million years ago, during the Pleistocene, when there was a network of rivers and lakes in the area. Many of these hand axes were recovered near the shoreline of an ancient body of water. “The Okwa Valley is an exceptionally challenging area for research,” said Mirosław Masojć of the University of Wrocław.

items.title: Tencent Open-Sources DFly2: Speculative Decoding That Reuses the Target’s Sparse KV Cache
items.summary: Tencent has open-sourced DFly2, a speculative decoding drafter built for natively sparse LLMs. DFly2 speculative decoding targets models like DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash and Tencent’s own Hy4 flash. Its main approach is that the drafter keeps no KV cache of its own. This is important for long-context and agentic serving, where draft memory competes with concurrency. TL;DR Size: 0.85B-parameter, 5-layer drafter shipped with Hy4 flash. Runs on: Serving tests used NVIDIA H20 GPUs with vLLM, TP8 per instance.

items.title: Ptolemaic Foundation Unearthed in Alexandria
items.summary: ALEXANDRIA, EGYPT— Ahram Online reports that a foundation made of limestone blocks, a tunnel, and a surrounding wall have been uncovered at the Shallalat Gardens site in the Royal Quarter of ancient Alexandria by researchers from the Hellenic Research Institute of Alexandrian Civilization (HRIAC). A committee of experts headed by Ayman Ashmawy of Egypt’s Supreme Council of Antiquities examined the square-shaped foundation and determined that it likely supported a tall building, which may have had a funerary function, based on the architectural features recovered at the site.

items.title: Researchers Evaluate Variety in Diet of Australia’s First Nations
items.summary: QUEENSLAND, AUSTRALIA—According to a statement released by the University of Queensland, Tiina Manne of the University of Queensland and her colleagues analyzed animal bones recovered at Barrow Island and Riwi, two archaeological sites in Western Australia. The study suggests that people consumed a wide variety of foods some 45,000 years ago. “On Barrow Island, which was then connected to the mainland, the diet included wallabies, turtles, and reef fish, and articulated bones suggest only the most nutritious parts were eaten and the rest were discarded,” Manne said.

items.title: Boeing to win lion’s share of Qantas widebody order over Airbus: Bloomberg
items.summary: Boeing is set to win the lion’s share of a potential Qantas widebody order over European rival Airbus, according to Bloomberg. On November 27, 2026, Bloomberg claimed that an order for 20 aircraft from the Australian flag carrier is set to include Boeing 787 Dreamliners and some Airbus A350s. The information is said to have been sourced from people with knowledge of developments involving the order. In a statement to Bloomberg, Qantas said: “We are still in discussion with the relevant aircraft manufacturers as part of our widebody fleet planning and no decisions have been made.”

items.title: The Best Single-Serve Coffee Maker for All the Pod People Out There (2026)
items.summary: Try as we might, there’s just no changing the hearts and minds of some people, even our dearest loved ones, by presenting them with inconvenient truths. I’m talking, of course, about people who prefer coffee from pods. But based on the popularity of coffee pod machines, it seems those of us who haven’t been assimilated into pod people are outnumbered. And, to be fair, even if the quality of their coffee is all over the place, we can’t deny their convenience. My goal here is to find single-serve coffee makers that can blend that convenience with coffee I actually want to drink.

items.title: Draining peatlands is responsible for a few percent of our global warming
items.summary: Much of the focus for human-caused climate change is on fossil fuels, which are creating most of our problems. But land use change is also a large component of the story, accounting for about one-third of total historical CO 2 emissions. Deforestation plays a major role here, but practices like draining wetlands also factor in. Exactly how much of our history of eliminating wetlands has contributed to warming is challenging to figure out. But thanks to new sources of data that measure emissions from today’s surviving wetlands, it’s possible to put a better number on it.

items.title: How the Sicilian Mafia Helped the Allies Invade Sicily in WWII
items.summary: Before Allied boots ever touched the beaches of Sicily during World War II, unlikely allies began planning together in New York. The United States needed help gaining every advantage possible to break through Axis positions in the Mediterranean, and its primary target was Sicily, a heavily fortified gateway to mainland Italy. To secure a successful landing, American naval intelligence turned to an unexpected resource: the American Mafia. What ensued was a partnership forged in the deep, tumultuous world of espionage that also influenced post-war Sicilian politics.

items.title: Arizona SNAP enrollment up slightly as food bank sees increased demand
items.summary: Even as enrollment in Arizonas federal food assistance program continues to tick up, St. Marys Food Bank is seeing increased demand. items.title: Could Science Have Been Different? Why Philosophers Cannot Agree
items.summary: Is scientific progress just a series of fortunate accidents, a contingent path determined by chance encounters and social influences? Or is it an inevitable march toward truth, a predetermined trajectory dictated by the very nature of reality? Looking at the history of science, it may seem as if it was laid out on a track of objective reality, so that our options were severely limited. As always, philosophers have found ways to both support and criticize this insight.

items.title: The Failure You Never Saw Coming
items.summary: Aviation is a world where pilots are constantly learning something new. We read textbooks, articles, and published stories, attend seminars and ground classes, and share experiences with other pilots. We use that knowledge on our next flight, trying to make flying as safe as possible. If a pilot ever says, “I know everything,” I believe that is when their professional growth ends. A friend and I recently spent some time discussing flight training, safety concerns, and some interesting experiences from our aviation careers.

items.title: American Airlines flight from San Diego to Chicago diverted to Phoenix Sky Harbor, passenger detained
items.summary: PHOENIX An American Airlines flight traveling from San Diego to Chicago was diverted to Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport overnight after air traffic controllers reported a "Level 3 threat" aboard the plane. Part of the draw is in how Rick and Morty utilizes the dynamic between the titular duo of a cynical, hard-drinking scientist and his grandson, and how it ruthlessly deconstructs every sci-fi trope from alien cultures to alternate universes. But while Rick and Morty is massively popular and influential, another series perfected its style, courtesy of Seth Rogen.

items.title: Psychological Horror Typing Game ‘Remote Control’ Launches January 29
items.summary: Canteen and publisher Weekend Games are tasking players with being on time next year for their shift at Plutus Corporation in the upcoming psychological horror typing game Remote Control. Coming to Steam on January 29, you can get a taste of what lies ahead with the demo that’s now available on the Steam page. Drawing inspiration from the sustained dread of Alien: Isolation and the dehumanizing psychological horror of Severance, Remote Control blends typing-driven gameplay that feels reminiscent of classic text-based adventure games, merged with recent hits like Mouthwashing and No, I’m Not a Human.

items.title: Run with the Semi-Wild Yilki Horses of Anatolia in Nur Tucker’s Captivating Photos
items.summary: Around the dusty plains and otherworldly volcanic rock formations of the historical region of Cappadocia, a millennia-old tradition continues. Here in Central Anatolia, Turkey, horses have been a part of daily life, civic programs, and military campaigns since prehistory. In The Untold Story of the Yilki Horse, photographer Nur Tucker captures a portrait of the region’s living heritage. Published by Hemeria, the title delves into the beauty and tenacity of the semi-wild horses while also highlighting the lifestyles of those who herd them through rugged landscapes.

items.title: The Cutthroat Business of Shipwrecks
items.summary: In 1627, treasures started to wash up on the beaches of France: diamonds, ebony, precious porcelain, spices, ivory, ambergris, and bezoars. Two Portuguese ships, so huge they were referred to as “ floating cities,” had shipwrecked off the coast of Bordeaux, spilling luxury goods into the waves. The disaster quickly threatened to become an international incident. The owners of the cargo (unsurprisingly) wanted their goods back—but the coast dwellers claimed that anything that washed up on shore was theirs by the ancient droit du naufrage, the “right of wreck.”

items.title: Listen to the Music of the Ancient World: From 40,000-Year-Old Flutes to Ancient Greek Songs
items.summary: There aren’t many ways to experience the ancient world. We can learn its languages, at least the ones that have left behind decipherable writings; we can behold its artifacts; we can visit its ruins. But nothing gets us quite as close to entering the consciousness of our distant forebears as hearing the music — or at least the sounds — that they did. In the new Archaeologist’s Notebook video above, Giselle Király gives us a tour through ancient musical history, explaining the instruments of those times that survive in one form or another today.

items.title: 7 Thanksgiving Horror Hits That Are Worth Being Thankful For
items.summary: There’s a certain sick satisfaction in taking holiday traditions’ comforting nature and turning it into the backdrop of murderous massacres. Halloween, Christmas, and even Valentine’s Day have received their share of horror films and subversive slashers that prey upon these holidays’ cozy customs. That said, it’s curious that Thanksgiving—the heavy-hitter between Halloween and Christmas—often goes overlooked when it comes to slasher inspiration. Thanksgiving may seem deceptively simple in comparison to Halloween and too close to Christmas’ family-based festivities.

items.title: Industry Groups Support Proposed Changes To Pilot Oxygen Rules
items.summary: Aviation groups are backing a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) proposal that would relax requirements for pilots to continuously wear supplemental oxygen masks at higher altitudes. In comments submitted to the FAA, the National Business Aviation Association (NBAA), the National Air Transportation Association (NATA), the Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association (AOPA) and Vertical Aviation International (VAI) backed proposed changes to oxygen requirements for pressurized aircraft operating under Parts 91 and 135.

items.title: Boeing’s Dave Schulte on why Southeast Asia will need 5,000 new jets by 2045
items.summary: Boeing said it expects Southeast Asia to need almost 5,000 new commercial airplanes over the next two decades. According to the planemaker’s 2026 Commercial Market Outlook (CMO), the region will take delivery of 4,985 new aircraft between 2026 and 2045, more than tripling its fleet from 1,475 aircraft to 5,215. items.title: Drones offer a new view of wildlife health. But what are they missing?
items.summary: Drones are transforming how scientists study wildlife, allowing researchers to photograph and measure animals in their natural environments, monitor larger populations and collect observations with less disturbance. While a photograph can reveal changes in an animal's size and shape, it cannot confidently tell researchers what those changes mean for its health.

items.title: My self-care ritual is a meal at a fancy restaurant - on my own
items.summary: "I think what is so special about solo dining is that you don't have to wait for people to make those plans. You can go out and do them yourself," says the 23-year-old. The self-confessed foodie is part of a growing trend of people booking tables for one - not because they're away with work but as a treat. items.title: Medicare Open Enrollment: Here’s What’s Changing, and What Mistakes To Avoid
items.summary: Annual open enrollment is underway for Medicare, the federal program that provides health insurance to roughly 70 million people. The coverage choices are complex and often consequential. Medicare provides health insurance to people 65 or older, as well as to some younger people with disabilities or certain health conditions. But it isn’t one plan. It’s more like a build-your-own-insurance menu. Roughly half of beneficiaries are enrolled in traditional Medicare, which consists of Parts A and B. Administered by the federal government, the plan covers hospital stays, skilled nursing care, doctor visits, outpatient care, and preventive screenings.

items.title: ‘There is no second river we can turn to’: Havasupai Tribe asks for investigation into high levels of arsenic in groundwater
items.summary: PHOENIX – A new analysis by the Grand Canyon Trust of 32 years of groundwater sampling across the Grand Canyon region showed that arsenic levels in monitoring wells near the Pinyon Plain uranium mine were uncharacteristically high. Four wells in the Coconino Aquifer tested positive for arsenic levels above safe drinking water levels in the Grand Canyon region, according to the trust. Three of the wells were at Pinyon Plain Mine, about 40 miles southeast of the Havasupai Indian Reservation, and one was at the Kaibab Plateau north of the Grand Canyon.

items.title: Where scientists draw the line on AI agents
items.summary: Delegating research tasks to AI does not remove scientists’ responsibility for how the work is accomplished. For example, a researcher using AI to review the literature needs to check whether the system overlooks conflicting evidence or makes claims the cited papers don’t support. Someone handing off data analysis to an agentic system needs to understand which methods it used, which files it accessed, and whether the results can be successfully reproduced.

items.title: Alaska Pilot Keeps Thanksgiving Turkey Drop Tradition Flying
items.summary: Alaska private pilot Esther Keim is continuing an annual Thanksgiving tradition of dropping frozen turkeys from a small airplane to families living off the road system in south-central Alaska. The operation, known as the Alaska Turkey Bomb, serves remote households around Skwentna, where residents rely on aircraft, boats and snowmachines to transport supplies. Reviving a Local Tradition Keim revived the holiday tradition in 2022 after learning that a local family had struggled to find food during the previous winter.

items.title: Faisal Islam: Why Trump's new tariffs are less of a threat

Instead there is something rather tentative about this latest exercise with talk of further negotiations. "We expect to have a broad, even a plurilateral negotiation to talk about excess capacity and how to resolve it," US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC. Around the world the view is that this week's announcement is an attempt to shore up the domestic legal underpinning of these tariffs, more than a fundamental change in the Trump trade agenda.

items.title: BAGSMART’s Pebble Switch Lets You Swap a Wheel, Not the Whole Suitcase
items.summary: A suitcase can come home with nothing worse than a scuff and still be a nuisance on the next trip if one wheel won’t turn. BAGSMART’s Pebble Carry-On Switch lets you replace the wheels yourself and comes with a spare set in a different color. The brighter wheels might be the reason you notice it, but they’re also parts you can keep for later. items.title: Friday Five with Nick Doyle: Seeing America Through Shades of Blue
items.summary: Creative minds can seemingly turn anything into art—from household items and food to packing supplies and bottle caps. For Los Angeles-born interdisciplinary artist Nick Doyle, the material of choice is denim. Even when working in other mediums, he often gravitates toward a denim-blue palette, as in his latest exhibition, “ Lonely but Free I’ll Be Found.” Presented at Pace Prints ’ New York gallery this fall, the exhibition marks Doyle’s first venture into printmaking, using graphic interpretations of everyday objects to examine American preoccupations with risk and reward, escapism, and the myth of the self-made man.

items.title: Easyjet Airbus A321neo Declares Emergency After Loud Bang Shakes Edinburgh
items.summary: EDINBURGH – An Edinburgh-bound emergency response was triggered on Thursday, November 26, after an easyJet (U2) Airbus A321neo operating from Edinburgh Airport (EDI) to London Gatwick Airport (LGW) declared a general emergency shortly after takeoff. The aircraft returned to Edinburgh after reports of a technical problem, while residents in the surrounding area reported hearing a loud bang as the aircraft climbed away from the airport. The flight, identified as EZY816, transmitted the international emergency transponder code Squawk 7700, prompting an emergency response at the Scottish airport.

items.title: New Dragon Ball Super Remake Is Hurting the Anime More Than Helping

items.title: ‘Good Tape’ Teaser: A Little Girl Builds a Box to Reach Her Dead Mother

items.title: The Australian Shuffle
items.summary: Shuffle a deck of cards and divide it into four packets. Pick up any packet, look at the top card, and remember it. Spell out the phrase AUSTRALIAN SHUFFLE, transferring one card from the top to the bottom of the packet for each letter. Now apply the phrase Down Under — put the top card down on the table, and the next card under the packet. Continue doing this until you’re holding a single card. It’s the card you memorized. ( By Josh Jay, based on a principle discovered by Alex Elmsley. )

items.summary: AirAsia Philippines is to cut jobs and scale back routes and flight frequencies, with high jet fuel prices and a weak peso driving up its operating costs. Local media has reported that about 90 captains and first officers have been told their employment will end on December 31, 2026. “AirAsia Philippines has made the very difficult decision to reduce our workforce. items.title: Novel Experiments Expand the Hunt for ‘Ultralight’ Dark Matter

items.title: American To Fly WWII Veterans to Pearl Harbor
items.summary: American Airlines said Tuesday that it will operate a charter flight to Hawaii next week carrying more than 85 World War II veterans, Rosie the Riveters and their guests to commemorate the 85th anniversary of the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor. Among those making the trip are military aviators, Medal of Honor recipients and two veterans who were living in Hawaii as teenagers at the time of the Dec. 7, 1941, attack. items.title: The Illustrated Version of “Alice’s Restaurant”: Watch Arlo Guthrie’s Thanksgiving Counterculture Classic

items.title: A cosmically close supernova may spill the stellar explosion’s secrets
items.summary: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback? Take our survey. (See our AI policy here.) When astronomers first spotted the supernova now designated SN 2026ahvu, it was just one of the dozens detected every day. But scientists soon realized this one was something very special, and they’ve been hustling to study it ever since. “I think almost everyone in the world is trying to trigger a telescope and look at this,” says astrophysicist Sumit Sarbadhicary of Johns Hopkins University. items.title: Macdonald Book Shop in Estes Park, Colorado
items.summary: At Macdonald Book Shop, a cozy and beloved store in the Colorado mountain town of Estes Park, selling books began as a side hustle. J. Edward Macdonald bought a small log cabin in Estes Park in 1908 and opened a hardware and general store next door — with one corner full of books for sale. When he retired, his wife Jessica turned the parlor of their home into a proper bookstore, also selling magazines, stationery, and school supplies. That was 1928. Books have been the focus ever since. Over the decades, the shop expanded to claim more of the original house.

It's too early to say much about the proof itself—mathematicians are still in the process of digesting it. But we can say a little about how the proof came about, and what it tells us about the state of math.

items.title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
items.summary: Most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them. However, the company is about to take a harder stance. Tidal announced that in the coming weeks, it will fully ban AI music because of the harm it does to human artists. Tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI. That wasn't enough to stem the tide of AI slop, though. Over the past 90 days, Tidal reports that 43 percent of new uploads were completely AI-generated.

items.title: Treasury CIO Is Vibe Coding a ‘Civilization’ Clone During Treasury Department Hack
items.summary: As the Treasury Department dealt with the fallout of a hack that took down some of its services, its Chief Information Officer was pushing updates to Legatum, his vibe coded Civilization clone. Sam Corcos is the cofounder of the A16z-backed glucose monitoring health startup called Levels; he became the Treasury Department’s Chief Information Officer as a DOGE hire near the beginning of Trump’s second term, and has been a leading AI evangelist within the administration since.
